item.title: Re: Hm.
item.content:encoded:
Fair enough, and I see the improvements have added some upvotes. Digestive sac… maybe. Let me check… ah, that would be a gastrovascular cavity (though "digestive sac" or "primitive gut" works, too). As for the antibody/sperm hybrid… hm…

(ponders)

Well, the gastrovascular cavity is normally seen in primitive creatures such as jellyfish and flatworms. If we follow through, that would make the SCP-274-2 roughly equivalent to the jellyfish's tentacles, especially since some varieties of jellyfish reproduce by budding from the tentacles. If you draw that comparison, the SCP-274-2 are effectively autonomous tentacles, with an occasional "bud tentacle" being sent out to propagate.

As for a lure, there are three methods of trapping prey that come to mind:

1. Bait. This can be anything from sound ("Help! Help! Someone help me! Help!") to a visual or even scent-based lure. After all, how often does the scent of fresh-baked chocolate chip cookies lead to danger… ?

2. Curiosity. When dealing with humans especially, the "non-bait bait". Flickering lights, strange sounds… heck, these things could almost live on parapsychologists alone.

3. Mechanical trap. Given the merging seen in SCP-274-2, it wouldn't be out of the question to have the "graffiti" simply reach out and grab passersby, pulling them into the wall to be absorbed. Or, of course, the "sidewalk graffiti" could act as a lue trap, or a trapdoor, or just an extended tentacle to reach out and gobble them up.

Just some thoughts.

item.content:encoded:
I've created my share of corrections here. I hope it helps.

1.
This doesn't need to be Keter. It seems easy to contain, and does not pose an immediate threat to the foundation or the world.
2.

MTF Alpha-9 is to set SCP-274-1 on fire,

Ordering personnel to "set it on fire" also sounds informal. Try using words such as torch, or demolish. Also, an entire Kilometer of buildings seems a bit drastic.
3.

Any apparatus used to contain or handle SCP-274 should either be incinerated, or entirely composed of metal or glass,

This isn't a pathogen. And I don't see why the foundation would use stone or plastic to torch a building.
4.

consistent with Krylon brand spray paint.

This can be easily interpreted as a reference to SCP-173, which could result in your article being downvoted straight to hell.
5.

SCP-274 will convert the interior of a wall into muscles, bones, and tendons, while the exterior acts as a protective shell and skin

It would be more interesting if SCP-274-1 moves the current material inside of itself to create a mechanical system, making it capable of imitating life and responding to stimuli. At least in my opinion.
6.

are lured into touching areas covered in SCP-274 due to its wet looking texture,

wat. The whole being lured into something because it's so fucking wet idea seems very odd. I'd recommend the art on the wall having a memetic effect that makes people want to explore the rest of the mural. THEN it would fit in with the possibility of being natural human curiosity.
7.

SCP-274-2 act as anti-bodies for SCP-274-1

This seems kind of lame and uncreative. It seems like you're basing the entire article on the photo, and not vice-verse. Try having the walls move and trap people or something like that.
8.

further cases of SCP-274-2 will leave SCP-274-1 and find a new building to spray with SCP-274

I like this idea, but not the idea of SCP-274-2. Perhaps the paint could be seen as coming from an unknown source, just appearing on the wall, only able to spread from a current mural.

All in all, it's a nice concept. Although we already have a few graffiti SCP's, I like the idea of this one more than the rest. With some work, it could be an amazing, artistic SCP.

item.title: Hm.
item.content:encoded:
Interesting. A few little things:

  • The picture should really be labeled in accordance with the table: SCP-274-1-4
  • I don't think you mean "sanitize". Technically, the SCP-274 being applied to the victim coats them, rather than removing microorganisms and dirt from their surface. You might get more mileage from the word "encapsulate". Or, since it's being sprayed into their mouths, you could assume an anesthetic effect that would make them easier to consume — much the way cytotoxic T cells begin killing the bacteria or virus before the NK cell moves in to consume the target they've "tagged".
  • Compulsions, even ones contracted by touch, are something of a sore point; if your creature or object has to have a compulsion in order to work, you might need to rewrite it. That's not to say there can never be a good SCP with a compulsion attached, but it works against you. Could the contaminated building pull in prey in another manner?
  • If SCP-274-2 don't have internal organs, they don't have a chest cavity; the "torso" area would be their center of mass, instead.
  • You may wish to make another proofreading pass. (I'd handle it myself, but I'm babysitting and using a weak connection right now.) You typed "contaminates" for "contaminants", for example.

As pertains to the reasons you cited:

1. The Foundation is less "above" and more "outside" the law. If you're a secret extra-governmental agency, you try to avoid people whose entire job description centers around finding out what's going on.

2. Noted, though as I said, the compulsion is working against you here.

3. Not all biological structures are organs. In most complex organisms, you pass through at least one preparatory structure (like the mouth and teeth in humans) before entering the actual digestive tract. And technically, if there's no waste and no need to chew, you don't need a digestive tract… the cell simply engulfs the target organism and digests it.

4. Technically, they're not antibodies; they're viruses. They work to infect surrounding organisms and convert them into additional instances, making them viral. Or, if you take a different tack, they're worker ants bringing food back to the colony.

You know, I really like the basic concept for this thing. Paint that turns a building into a living being with spray-painting entities spreading the effect is really cool.

But I don't know if the SCP really needs to be "alive" in the strict biological sense. I'm not really an expert in biology, but some of the science behind this article seems a bit off, particularly the part about the giant unicellular SCP-274-2.

Maybe you could remove the bits referring to SCP-274 with terms assuming that it is some sort of actual organism (e.g. SCP-274-2 being a unicellular organism, the mitosis, etc.)? We have plenty of SCPs that would be considered "alive" without necessarily having a discernible/based-in-real-life-science biochemistry; some aren't even made of physical matter.
